scores.reason: Random plasma C-peptide with a concurrent glucose is a routine automated immunoassay on all major platforms with no timed protocol, and the decision thresholds (80, 200, 600 pmol/L) are wide relative to assay disagreement. It is not fully standardized (inter-system CV 24.5% in one 94-laboratory Chinese survey, 5.7% after recalibration; a JCTLM-listed ID-LC-MS/MS procedure and WHO reagent 13/146 exist), so it sits on the 2/3 boundary; scored 3 because the values are used far from the cutoffs for most patients and sampling is simple. Measure type: C-peptide, random (non-fasting) with concurrent glucose.

scores.reason: Insulin (with C-peptide and glucose) must be drawn at the nadir during symptoms or during a timed mixed-meal test, and the insulin immunoassay is not standardized: twelve current immunoassays differed from an ID-MS comparator by about -298 to +303 pmol/L, and analogue cross-reactivity varies by platform. Widely available but unstandardized and timed, so 2; no assay-specific threshold exists for this use. Measure type: post-load or mixed-meal / symptomatic-nadir insulin (with C-peptide).

scores.reason: HOMA-IR needs one fasting insulin and glucose draw, which is simple and routine to order, but insulin assays are unstandardized, HOMA-IR values for the same sera ranged about twofold across 11 assays, and IRIS had to use central laboratories because insulin is not standardized. A fixed threshold of 3.0 therefore does not transfer across assays; widely available but unstandardized gives 2. Measure type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: A cross-platform check on US-marketed C-peptide assays at the 200 and 600 pmol/L decision thresholds, with recalibration to a commutable reference material, so classification does not depend on the assay.
path_to_viability.basis: Recalibration cut inter-system CV from 24.5% to 5.7% (PMID 35177563); commutable materials and a JCTLM-listed reference procedure exist (PMIDs 37141618, 38549041); no US cross-platform study was found in the screened records.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: An assay-specific, validated insulin threshold for post-bariatric hypoglycaemia from a standardized mixed-meal protocol, on insulin assays traceable to a commutable reference material.
path_to_viability.basis: No accepted insulin threshold (PMID 30101281, per project files); insulin assays disagree and no JCTLM-listed insulin reference procedure or certified reference material (PMID 40802520, author statement).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: An assay-harmonized HOMA-IR (or insulin) threshold, with the IRIS 3.0 value mapped to current assays, or a guideline wording that names the assay requirement.
path_to_viability.basis: HOMA-IR differs about twofold across assays (PMID 18535197); no commutable insulin reference material (PMID 40802520); IRIS used central laboratories (PMC4887756 via project files).

anchor_issues: Row 6 D4: anchors 2 and 3 overlap for a routine automated assay that is widely available but not fully standardized (C-peptide). Chose 3 because there is no timed protocol and thresholds are wide relative to assay disagreement; a strict reading of 'unstandardized' gives 2.

Row 5 D4: the anchor mixes assay quality and protocol burden; a timed symptomatic-nadir or mixed-meal protocol on an unstandardized insulin assay was scored 2 as the anchor describes. No anchor separates 'timed protocol' from 'unstandardized'.
Row 13 D4: a single fasting draw is easy but the threshold is assay-dependent; no anchor says how to weigh ease of sampling against unstandardized assay. Chose 2.
The D4 anchor does not say whether to score the assay as currently marketed in the US or as studied; most inter-assay data here come from China, Korea and Europe or older assay generations.
assumptions: Scored the US setting; no US cross-platform data were found for C-peptide, so non-US surveys (China, Korea) were used and flagged as medium confidence.
Row 6 measure was read as random plasma C-peptide with concurrent glucose, as in usecases-verified.md; urine C-peptide:creatinine ratio was noted as an alternative, not scored.
Row 5 measure was read as insulin (with C-peptide and glucose) at symptomatic nadir or during a mixed-meal test.
Setting tags were assigned by judgement from the use description and are outside the D4 scope.

Older-generation figures (Marcovina 2007, Manley 2008) may not apply to current platforms; Rohlfing 2025 and Zhou 2022 are the current-generation anchors.
